response.answer: RIDE TWINPIG 2027 SNOWBOARD — COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT FACT SHEET IDENTITY & MANUFACTURER 1. Brand: Ride Snowboards [1] 2. Model name: Twinpig [1] 3. Model year: 2027 (Southern Hemisphere season designation; equivalent to 2025/2026 Northern Hemisphere season product cycle — see note on naming convention below) [2] 4. Product type: Snowboard [1] 5. Manufacturer founded: September 1992 in Redmond, WA [3] 6. Parent company: Elevate Outdoor Collective (formerly K2-MDV Holdings), headquartered in Seattle, WA [4] 7. Parent company subsidiaries include: K2 Skis, K2 Snowboards, Marker, Dalbello, Völkl, RIDE Snowboards, LINE Skis, and others [4] 8. K2 acquired Ride in 1997 for eighteen million dollars [5] 9. Ride Snowboards has over 30 years of experience in building high-quality products [6] 10. Manufacturing location: China (production factory), with R&D/prototyping in Seattle, WA headquarters [7][8] 11. Model first available: The Twinpig was first introduced for the 2019 season as a twin-shaped derivative of the Warpig [9] 12. Design origin: Twin redesign of the Warpig — the Twinpig is a twin version of Ride's most popular WARPIG model [1] 13. Construction tweaks were made in 2022; construction remained similar from 2022 through 2025 [10] 14. Gender target: Unisex — this product is designed without a gender fit in mind [11] DISAGREEMENT: Camber Profile Description 15. Camber type (manufacturer 2026 site — evo.com): "Twin Standard Camber — A true twin shape hybrid profile that has more camber than rocker" [12] 16. Camber type (The House / older Ride description / getboards 2024): "Twin Standard Camber — A true twin shape hybrid profile that has more rocker than camber" [13][14] 17. Camber type (merchant source): Standard Camber — camber throughout with extended rocker zones in tip and tail [2] 18. Camber type (BaseNZ 2027): "Twin Hybrid Rocker profile blends camber pop with rocker pressability" [15] *COMMENT: There is a clear disagreement between sources on whether the Twinpig has "more camber than rocker" or "more rocker than camber." The most recent evo/Ride official 2026 page says "more camber than rocker." The older sources and some retailers say "more rocker than camber." The 2027 BaseNZ listing calls it "Twin Hybrid Rocker." The manufacturer's own site appears to have changed the language across model years. Buyer should confirm directly with manufacturer.* SHAPE & DESIGN 19. Shape: Asymmetrical Twin [1][2] 20. Twin shape description: Same shape on the nose and tail — great for going both directions, park riding, going switch [1] 21. Asymmetric sidecut: Improves heelside turn initiation and control with different radii for the heel and toeside edges [1] 22. Sidecut type: Asymmetrical Quadratic Sidecut — blending of three radii to improve turn initiation/exit while providing the best grip possible [1] 23. Volume shifted design: The Twinpig is short/wide and designed to be sized down 3–6 cm from your standard twin [1] 24. Wider than traditional twin: The Twinpig isn't as wide as the Warpig, but it's still wider than a traditional twin shape [1] 25. Width options: Standard and Wide available [2] 26. Double-blunted tips [12] 27. Setback: 0 mm (all sizes) — centered stance [1] FLEX & RESPONSE 28. Flex rating (merchant): Soft [2] 29. Flex rating (Ride official): Response = Mellow [1] 30. Flex feel on snow (SnowboardingProfiles review): Medium (5.5/10) — felt stiffer than promoted [16] 31. Torsional flex (EatGoldSnow review): Medium/soft, with overall flex medium/stiff [17] 32. Flex rating (BaseNZ 2027): Medium (4/10) [15] *COMMENT: Multiple sources disagree on the flex — Ride says "Mellow," merchant says "Soft," BaseNZ says "Medium 4/10," and one reviewer says it felt stiffer than expected at 5.5/10 on snow.* 33. Flex direction: True twin — symmetrical flex nose to tail [1] CONSTRUCTION & MATERIALS 34. Core material: Performance™ Core — Aspen, Bamboo, and Paulownia wood blend [1][12] 35. Fiberglass: Hybrid Glass — Triaxial on top, biaxial on base; balanced torsional flex and stiffness [12][13] 36. Sidewall: Slim Walls — 3D composite structure over Slimewall® material for efficient energy transfer, lighter weight, and better damping [1] 37. Slimewall material: Urethane-based, forgiving and ductile, absorbing impacts; virtually indestructible per manufacturer claim [18] 38. Impact protection: Double Impact Plates — two-layer urethane weaves beneath each binding area to improve compressive strength and prevent board breaks [1] 39. Base: Sintered, Stone Ground 4000 PTEX — more durable, harder, and faster than extruded [1] 40. Edge material: Cleave Edge™ Steel — nearly 50% more steel, delivers resistance to edge cracking, can be detuned to larger radii [1] 41. Edge recycled content: 30% recycled steel materials [1] 42. Resin: Bio Resin — plant-based epoxy from renewable resources [1] 43. Factory wax: Wend® Meadowfoam Biodegradable Wax — made from wildflower seeds native to California and Oregon; non-toxic and completely biodegradable [1] 44. Topsheet (merchant): Topless Topsheet — graphics transferred directly to fiberglass [2] 45. Topsheet (Ride official 2026): Standard Top Sheet — durable urethane top sheet material [13] *COMMENT: Merchant says "Topless Topsheet" while the 2025/26 Ride official page says "Standard Top Sheet." Older model years (2019) used Topless Construction. The 2027 model's topsheet style should be confirmed.* 46. Mounting pattern: 2x4 inserts [2] 47. Carbon stringers (BaseNZ 2027 description): Carbon Array 3 stringers — maximize pop and control [15] 48. Tip/tail construction: Thin Con — tapered tips and tails for reduced swing weight, improved tip flex, and boosted overall durability [2] SUSTAINABILITY 49. Bio Resin: Plant-based epoxy from renewable resources reduces carbon emissions [1] 50. Edges: 30% recycled steel [1] 51. Packaging: FSC® Certified Materials for base stickers and shipping boxes [1] 52. Factory solar energy: 44% of production energy from sustainable solar sources [1] AVAILABLE SIZES & SPECS (from Ride official size chart) 53. Available sizes: 136cm, 142cm, 148cm, 151cm, 154cm, 156W, 157cm [1] 54. Effective edge (148cm): 1085 mm [1] 55. Waist width (148cm): 257 mm [1] 56. Tip/Tail width (148cm): 307 mm [1] 57. Reference stance (148cm): 533 mm (21 inches) [1] 58. Rider weight range (148cm): 100–205 lbs / 45–93 kg [1] 59. Effective edge (151cm): 1110 mm [1] 60. Waist width (151cm): 263 mm [1] 61. Tip/Tail width (151cm): 314 mm [1] 62. Reference stance (151cm): 533 mm (21 inches) [1] 63. Rider weight range (151cm): 130–210 lbs / 59–95 kg [1] 64. Effective edge (154cm): 1123 mm [1] 65. Waist width (154cm): 268 mm [1] 66. Tip/Tail width (154cm): 320 mm [1] 67. Reference stance (154cm): 559 mm (22 inches) [1] 68. Rider weight range (154cm): 140–220+ lbs / 64–100+ kg [1] 69. Effective edge (157cm): 1148 mm [1] 70. Waist width (157cm): 270 mm [1] 71. Tip/Tail width (157cm): 323 mm [1] 72. Reference stance (157cm): 559 mm (22 inches) [1] 73. Rider weight range (157cm): 160–220+ lbs / 73–100+ kg [1] 74. Effective edge (156W): 1136 mm [1] 75. Waist width (156W): 275 mm [1] 76. Tip/Tail width (156W): 328 mm [1] 77. Reference stance (156W): 559 mm (22 inches) [1] 78. Rider weight range (156W): 170–220+ lbs / 77–100+ kg [1] SIZING & FIT GUIDANCE 79. Volume shift sizing: Size down 3–6 cm from your standard twin [1] 80. Recommended boot sizes per size (TheGoodRide): 148: US 8–9, 151: US 9–10, 154: US 10–11, 157: US 11–12, 156W: US 11.5–12.5+ [19] 81. Stance requirement: Requires riding perfectly duck and centered for optimal asymmetric effect [19] TERRAIN & USE CASE 82. Board category (merchant): All Mountain [2] 83. Specialty (Ride official): All Mountain, Park [1] 84. Terrain: Park, groomers, powder [2] 85. Riding style: Freestyle, carving, switch riding [2] 86. Ability level (Ride official): Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced [1] 87. Ability level (merchant): Intermediate [2] 88. Ability level (Absolute Snow): Intermediate to Advanced [20] PRICING & AVAILABILITY 89. USD MSRP: $569.95 (2025/2026 model — current Ride official sale price $398.97) [1] 90. AUD price (merchant provided): $899.99 AUD [2] 91. NZD price (BaseNZ): $1,099.99 NZD regular, $989.99 NZD sale [21] 92. USD price at The House: $398.95 [19] 93. USD price at Christy Sports: $398.97 [19] 94. USD price at Salty Peaks (2025/26): $675.00 [22] 95. EUR price at Blue Tomato: €429.00 [19] 96. Availability (merchant): Preorder, estimated availability May 1, 2026 [2] 97. Availability at evo (2025/26 model): In stock now [23] 98. Availability at BaseNZ (2027): Sold Out (all sizes) [21] 99. Availability at Rhythm Snowsports AU (2027): Listed, sizes 151/154/156W [11] RETAILER LISTING 100. Ride Snowboards direct (ridesnowboards.com) — official manufacturer store, strong reputation [1] 101. evo.com — major US specialty retailer, price match guarantee, 1-year returns, free shipping [23] 102. The House (the-house.com) — established US online snowboard shop, 90-day return policy [13] 103. Tactics (tactics.com) — reputable US board shop, free shipping over $150, low price guarantee [24] 104. BaseNZ (basenz.com) — NZ specialty retailer with free NZ shipping [21] 105. Rhythm Snowsports (rhythmsnowsports.com.au) — Australian specialty retailer, 14-day refund/365-day exchange, Rhythm Membership for 10% off [11] 106. Melbourne Snowboard Centre (melbournesnowboard.com.au) — Australian retailer, 30-day return credit [2] 107. Salty Peaks — US snowboard shop based in Salt Lake City [22] 108. Amazon — available but limited model years [25] 109. Christy Sports — US chain snowboard retailer [19] 110. ERIK'S Bike Board & Ski — US multi-sport retailer [26] WARRANTY 111. Warranty: 3-year manufacturer warranty from time of purchase [24] REVIEW SCORES & OPINIONS 112. SnowboardingProfiles score: 81.1 out of 100 — ranked 28th out of 33 all-mountain-freestyle boards tested [16] 113. TheGoodRide: Extended demo over 10+ days; reviewer liked it so much they asked to keep it [19] 114. Reviewer impression (SnowboardingProfiles): Board felt stiffer than expected; not super forgiving of skidded turns; intermediate friendly, not beginner friendly [16] 115. Carving opinion (SnowboardingProfiles): Decent on a carve but nothing epic; had a feeling it wanted to revert flat [16] 116. Turning feel (TheGoodRide): Fun turn, love the sidecut; slow to initiate but fun once engaged [19] 117. Buttering (TheGoodRide): Super easy to butter [19] 118. Switch riding (TheGoodRide): Just as easy either way; asymmetrical twins are great for this [19] 119. Pop/Jumps (TheGoodRide): Really poppy feel underfoot; good air from an ollie [19] 120. Edge hold (TheGoodRide): Pretty competent edge hold but not the strongest quality; lets go a bit on harder snow [19] 121. Speed (TheGoodRide): Not a bomber; fast enough for moderate mountain speed [19] 122. Base speed (TheGoodRide): Decent base but not an ultra glider when waxed; adequate for moderate speeds [19] 123. Weight (SnowboardingProfiles): One of the heaviest boards weighed out of ~100 models; felt heavy on snow [16] 124. Weight (TheGoodRide): Feels on the light side of normal for this width — disagreement with SnowboardingProfiles [19] *COMMENT: TheGoodRide and SnowboardingProfiles disagree on weight perception. TheGoodRide found it "light side of normal" while SnowboardingProfiles found it "one of the heaviest." Different model years may explain this (2019 vs 2022).* 125. Powder performance (forum user): Not a powder-specific board, but for a park-oriented board does well in powder if bindings are set far back [27] 126. Powder performance (SnowboardingProfiles): Struggled in deeper powder; sank under snow and required effort to keep nose afloat [16] 127. Emotional attachment (EatGoldSnow reviewer): Rider was "obsessed" and "emotionally attached" after first lap [17] 128. Park impression (Whitelines): "If you're looking to go HAM in the park this might be the board for you" — ideal for intermediate riders looking to work on park skills [28] 129. Durability impression (Whitelines): Rock-solid dependability; Double Impact Plates, full steel edges, and durable sintered base handle park abuse [28] 130. Forum user negative opinion: One forum user found the 154 Twinpig not that impressive; lacking pop compared to other boards; washed out in harder snow [29] COMPETITOR COMPARISONS 131. Related model: Ride Warpig — directional version in the same Pig series; more freeride oriented [1] 132. Comparable competitor: YES Greats — reviewed side by side by TheGoodRide; Greats carves exceptionally well for a freestyle board [19][30] 133. Comparable competitor: K2 Niseko Pleasures — more nimble and lighter in powder compared to Twinpig [16] 134. Comparable competitor: Never Summer Proto Type Two — wider stance option; considered by forum users as alternative [29] 135. Comparable competitor: Bataleon Evil Twin — 3BT technology offers different ride feel; freestyle twin alternative [31] 136. Other comparable boards mentioned in forum discussions: Burton Custom FV, Jones Mountain Twin, YES Typo, Capita Defenders of Awesome [30][31] ADDITIONAL NOTABLE ATTRIBUTES 137. Recommended stance: Duck stance, centered [19] 138. Best suited rider: Someone riding freestyle over the mountain who wants something shorter, with surface area for stable landings and speed when flat basing [16] 139. Board is not recommended for: Riders who prioritize big directional carves or speed bombing [17][19] 140. Binding compatibility: Compatible with Re:Flex and standard disc mounting systems [11]
